A continuous catalytic reactor unit running a fixed-bed hydrogenation has seen reactor conversion fall about 20% over the past month, staying low run after run. The decline followed a switch to a new feedstock supplier after a routine catalyst reload. The process team's leading theories are that the reactor is running too cool or at the wrong pressure, so they favor retuning temperature and pressure. Effluent analysis has shown a slightly elevated byproduct fraction. Routine unit data read broadly within range. The feed, temperature, purification, and regeneration systems are all adjustable, and polishing and regeneration options are available. You have a limited number of experiments; you may measure quantities and apply available controls or treatments, alone or in combination. Determine what is really driving the loss and what to do about it.

OUTCOME OF INTEREST: ConversionEfficiency (higher_is_better)
BUDGET: 0/15 experiments used, 15 left (code is free).
TURNS: 0/32, 32 left. Interventions so far: 0.
data files for code: (none yet)
MEASURABLE SIGNALS (ids):
  m0: conversion efficiency
  m1: reactor pressure
  m2: inlet temperature
  m3: quench flow
  m4: preheater duty
  m5: recycle-gas purity
  m6: bed pressure drop
  m7: feed moisture
  m8: catalyst surface area
  m9: catalyst particle size
  m10: bed height
  m11: purge rate

CONTROLS (ids):
  a0: set recycle-gas purity range [0, 100]
  a1: inlet temperature range [0, 100]
  a2: set feed moisture range [0, 100]
  a3: set preheater duty range [0, 100]
  a4: set catalyst particle size range [0, 100]
  a5: set purge rate range [0, 100]
  a6: set bed pressure drop range [0, 100]

RESULT OF LAST ACTION
(none yet)

YOUR MEMORY
(empty)
